feedback: Written before this geometry has raced. Iterations 0 to 3 show that max_error sat at 0.0609 to 0.0618 on every track in every design, and oval progress stayed at 0.115 whatever the span, footprint, lookahead, or wheel_track (iteration 3 matched iteration 2 exactly). Line losses went from 1 to 0 when the span moved from ±0.04 to ±0.06 (iteration 2), so the span controls sensing. Slalom progress fell from 0.105 to 0.035 over the same change. I kept the controller stable across these runs, so the only things that moved the result were sensing span and track, and neither moved the floor. What I had to do in the controller: keep the sign-proportional weights [-2,-1,0,1,2] because the signal stayed smooth across every span, and hold base_speed at 1.6 because a wider wheel radius speeds the robot up. Next race: if line_loss_events stay at 0 and max_error on oval and s-bend falls below about 0.058, keep wheel_radius 0.035 and try span ±0.055 to recover more slalom progress. If line_loss_events rise above 0 with ±0.05, go back to ±0.06 and accept the slalom cost. If max_error stays at about 0.061 with wheel_radius 0.035, the floor is not a radius effect, so test mass 0.6 next, as the Integrator's learning note suggests.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events stay at 0 with ±0.05 and max_error on oval and s-bend drops below about 0.058, keep wheel_radius 0.035 and try outer sensors at ±0.055, because iteration 2 (±0.06) had 0 line losses and iteration 1 (±0.04) reached slalom progress 0.110.
If line_loss_events rise above 0 with ±0.05, return the outer sensors to ±0.06 at y = 0.03 with wheel_radius 0.035, since iteration 1 showed a loss at ±0.04 and iteration 2 showed none at ±0.06.

If max_error stays at about 0.061 with wheel_radius 0.035, keep the span and try mass 0.6 kg, because iterations 0 to 3 show that span, track and lookahead did not move the floor and mass is the untested geometry lever.
